newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suez, Lyonnaise open sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Suez, Lyonnaise open sharply higher.

text.p: Shares in French holding company Cie de Suez and utilities group Lyonnaise des Eaux opened sharply higher on Monday following newspaper reports the two were preparing a merger.
Suez shares opened up 3.42 percent at 290 francs per share, while Lyonnaise shares started 2.67 percent higher at 576 francs.

Spokeswomen for the two companies earlier declined comment on a report in Le Monde newspaper on Saturday that the Suez and Lyonnaise chairmen wanted to make rapid progress to conclude a merger ahead of a Suez board meeting on April 1.
It said the two men were expected to work on the plan this weekend.

Talk of a planned merger has already run into criticism in Belgium, which fears that Belgian national interests would be threatened by any takeover by Lyonnaise of its utilities group Tractebel, owned by Suez's Belgian subsidiary Societe Generale de Belgique.

Financial weekly Investir on Friday reported that Compagnie Generale des Eaux (CGE) was considering a hostile bid for Suez to block the merger with its rival Lyonnaise. But a source close to the group said that an acquisition of Suez was not in line with CGE's strategy.
